title: External comparison: Causal Fermion Systems share carrier and universality class with QOU but are a distinct continuum theory
html:
Causal fermion systems (CFS), developed by Felix Finster, Niky Kamran, and Marco Oppio [finster2021], Felix Finster, Maximilian Jokel, and Claudio F. Paganini [finster2022], and Felix Finster, Johannes Kleiner, and Claudio F. Paganini [finster2024], provide a parallel continuum unification programme in which spacetime points are finite-rank self-adjoint operators x, y on a Hilbert space \mathcal{H}. Translating both frameworks into tracial non-commutative probability places their spectral functionals on a common footing.

Structural agreements

  1. Common tracial comparison carrier. While CFS acts natively on bounded finite-rank spinor operators in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}), restricting to finite-dimensional normalized spectral traces embeds both operator algebras into finite type II_1 factors for direct comparison.
  2. Asymptotic free-probability universality class. Under large-rank Plancherel scaling of Philippe Biane [biane1998], the tracial moments of both frameworks lie in the free-probability universality class.
  3. Common commutative-shadow data type. The traceful Plancherel projection maps non-commutative algebraic data to a commutative spectrum measure.

Structural differences

QOU evaluates the Frobenius Gram pairing G(x, y) := \mathrm{tr}_M(x \cdot y), whereas the CFS causal action principle [finster2021, finster2022, finster2024] evaluates symmetric functions of the absolute-value differences |\lambda_i^{xy}| - |\lambda_j^{xy}| of the 2n non-trivial eigenvalues of the operator product x y.

This yields three functional mismatches:

  • Pointwise mismatch. G(1, 1) = 1, whereas identical eigenvalue magnitudes give \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CFS}}(1, 1) = 0.
  • Integral mismatch. G is odd under x \mapsto -x, whereas \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CFS}} depends on |\lambda_i^{xy}| and is even.
  • Spectral-variance decomposition. Expanding the normalized pairwise squared difference \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CFS}}^{(\mathrm{norm})}(x, y) := \frac{1}{4n^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^{2n}\bigl(|\lambda_i^{xy}| - |\lambda_j^{xy}|\bigr)^2 = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|\lambda_i^{xy}|^2 - \bigl(\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^{2n}|\lambda_i^{xy}|\bigr)^2 rewrites the CFS dispersion directly as G_2(x, y) - \lVert x \cdot y\rVert_1^{\,2} in normalized Schatten moments.

Unresolved numerical question

Whether the higher-moment spectral variance vanishes or crosses at q_0 \approx 1.1100 has not been established.

Corollary for QOU

The QOU phenomena (knot topology, braid statistics) are pre-projection algebra data. They lie outside any commutative-shadow framework.
